authority_statement: Informational report only; the deterministic LFighter pipeline retains all security decision authority.
executive_summary: Observed DDoS-to-Benign prediction rates were lower in the defended branch than the plain attack branch; reconstruction reduced attribution distance toward the paired preattack reference.

facts.statement: The plain attack mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.155131, versus 0.040246 in the paired clean branch.
The defended mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.052335, an absolute reduction of 0.102796 from the plain attack branch.
Mean malicious recall was 0.975000, minimum malicious recall was 0.900000, and maximum benign false-positive rate was 0.000000.
Normalized attribution distance decreased from 0.807118 to 0.484905, with recovery fraction 0.399214.

interpretations.statement: Observed prediction behavior is consistent with targeted suppression of DDoS predictions toward the Benign class, but does not establish malicious intent.
Reconstruction moved the attribution profile toward its paired preattack clean reference; this is not evidence of oracle clean restoration.

refusals: Refuse to assert malicious intent: verified malicious intent is unsupported.
Refuse to claim oracle clean recovery: exact oracle clean recovery is unsupported.
uncertainties: The clean attribution comparator is the paired round 4 preattack reference rather than an oracle clean state.
Rejected and oracle-clean attribution states were unavailable.
Per-client detector scores and numeric detector thresholds were not present.
Evidence is limited to development and validation; reserved test arrays remained closed.
